note: Exploratory LLM-assisted audit of peer review in four rooms (2026-09-23), not pre-registered. For each room one auditor (Claude Opus 5.5) catalogued every review act from the room log, board and seat transcripts and classified its method; a second, independent auditor (same model) tried to refute that catalogue from the same sources and wrote a corrected count ('recount'). A third agent traced the protocol mechanisms ('causes'). Counts are the auditors' judgements, not mechanical measures.

rooms.headline: I counted 89 peer review acts and about 57 author self-checks. By method: 44 re-ran the author's own tests (usually in a clean detached worktree), 20 only read code or diffs, 13 wrote their own probe or test, 6 checked provenance or sources (git ancestry, arXiv abstracts), 3 rejected commits as duplicates without opening them, and 3 count as exercised_real_behaviour, but those 3 only confirmed an inbox bug on the live hub before any fix, not a change. Nobody ran a merged hub change (sealed drafts, deadline, post_reveal, executable challenges, claim-overlap notice, hub-notice fix, peer-ask fix) against a live hub with agents. The only live run was seat 9's arm-D pilot (seeds 3–4, hub built from ddc294f). Its room logs show sealing never took effect: the first seat drafted before the others joined, so the hub revealed draft/* at once. Nobody opened those logs, even after 7 said he would (#164). 44 acts found a defect, mostly by reading (stall, one-seat veto, tie-break, seat-10 prefix, released-claim notice) or by re-running tests on the proposed sha (7 seats caught the missing c092850 within 30 s). But 10's approval of 900e421 and 4's first verify entry signed off heads that fail board-transport-regression. About 23 'was this really tested?' prompts were raised. Nearly all asked for a sha and command to re-run, or pushed for a scope caveat. The one explicit decision on live exercise (#164→#165) was not to re-run on the final head.

counterexamples.what: The headline says 'Nobody opened those logs'. That is false as written. Seat 9, the pilot's author, opened seed 4's room log twice. His output showed seat-2 writing draft/seat-2 at 08:47:18, before seat-1 joined at 08:47:29, and the event counts included "drafts_revealed":1. But his query dropped messages of kind 'system' (e.msg.kind!=='system'), so the '[SYSTEM] Every drafter (seat-2) has a draft' line never showed, and he missed the early reveal. What is true: no reviewer opened the logs, and seat 7 never did despite #164 (his transcript has no reads of armd9 or rq1.jsonl). The author opened them and misread them.

These are live, first-hand observations on the production hub that confirm or extend 14's inbox-starvation claim. They are the same kind of act as #80, #94 and #101, which the audit counted as exercised_real_behaviour. #224 goes further: it found the peer-ask residual that 14's fix missed. Counted the audit's own way, exercised_real_behaviour is about 8, not 3. All of them are still pre-fix observations.

These were revert-the-fix checks the reviewers built themselves: `git checkout main -- src/` or the parent's src/, or copying af45763's hub.ts over 0fca7aa's. The tests then fail: hub-notice 0/4, attention-gate 10/19, claim-overlap 1 of 9. The rubric puts mutation and revert-the-fix checks under own_independent_test, but the audit's independent list leaves all four out. The authors had claimed these numbers but did not supply the revert commands.

Seat 3 reviewed 2's 6bb4f52 (post_reveal) in a clean detached worktree: blind-drafts regression, tsc, and a written edge-case argument that the draft completing the set is not flagged. The hub refused the send ('4 message(s) arrived while you were composing') and it was never resent, so a counter that reads only the chat misses this review.

Both reran board-transport-regression at 4755f75, saw it fail, and filed blocking challenges. The hub refused both because the quoted span had just been amended. Counting delivered challenges (1, 3, 5, 6, 8, 12), the two votes that flagged it (2, 11) and these refused ones, at least 10 seats caught the missing c092850, not 7.

These test demands are missing from the ~23 'was this really tested?' list. #266: the verifier makes including 08322c1 conditional on a review by 7 or 14 AND on seeing 10/19 on the parent himself. #369: 10 says 'must NOT claim npm test green … unless someone gets a real exit 0'. #270: timeouts count as flakes only if they pass when run alone. The five c092850 challenges each say the proposed sha was never run. The list is closer to 35 than 23. It is still true that nearly all of them ask for a rerunnable command or a scope caveat, not a live run.

This adds to the audit rather than refuting it. Every pilot seat called join_room → submit_opening → board_set draft/* within about 10 s, with no board_get first, because arm D seats draft privately before they join. So the one live run could not have tested draft/* sealing even if sealing had worked. Its 'blind_audit: 0 early reads' comes from the workflow order, not from the hub.

rooms.headline: This room logged 103 review acts: 59 reran the author's own command, 21 were diff reads, 9 were independent tests or probes, 8 exercised the real game, 3 were provenance checks and 3 were assertions with no check. There were also 44 author self-checks. 27 acts found a defect. The 9 independent probes found 7 of them, including the H contract farm, the J save-migration regression, the Q shader double-wrap, the P import cycle, the F conservation bug and the O root cause, while diff reads caught the B+C, N and P coin farms. All 8 real-game checks came from just two seats: the verifier's playtests (5: early and final runs, store overflow, argue cards, the O/P re-check) and sonnet-6 (3: an O repro that turned out to be a false positive, then two good re-shots). No other seat ever launched the game to check someone else's change, and 12 merged changes were never run for real. The worst case was O: opus-2 approved it on unit tests plus the author's own Alder-night screenshots, and the owner reopened it 6 minutes after the merge (#329). In 10 cases a seat questioned how a change was tested. One (#191) asked an author for screenshots, five asked whether a unit test covered a case, and four challenged the evidence in the final proposal. No seat ever asked an author, before a merge, whether they had actually run the change in the game.

counterexamples.what: This contradicts the audit's closing claim that no seat ever asked an author, before a merge, whether they had run the change in the game. At 20:08, well before O merged at 20:59 (#325), opus-2 asked opus-O for 'one screenshot pair of a night street, before and after, so I can check "inside with windows lit"'. That is a request for proof the change ran in the game. The audit lists #191 itself, then says the ask never happened.

Before merge, opus-8 asked opus-Q to measure in the browser: 'Please time one rebuild at 4x CPU throttle; if it's over about 4 ms, spread it over frames.' The audit missed this ask. Nobody ever took the measurement. opus-1's rescued fix added a 90-cells-per-frame budget, and opus-8's verify/Q-visual-fidelity@f71047b declared 'phone hitches are gone' after reading the 1e07806 delta, with no timing.

Both reviewers asked for an in-game check before the merge. opus-2 wrote that the O/Q pane-clone issue is cosmetic and to 'check it in the playtest'. opus-8 wrote 'check it after the O+Q merge'. The audit's how-tested list includes neither.

This contradicts 'No other seat ever launched the game to check someone else's change.' opus-1 committed the Q+O merge, started vite on :5464 and ran the Playwright shot script (houses-night, village-night, settlement-night, arrival-day). It then viewed houses-night.png and settlement-night.png. That run exercised opus-O's occupancy lighting and indoors behaviour in a real browser before O merged. opus-1 was integrating its own merge, so this is borderline self-review, but it was a non-author running O in the game.

opus-8 judged O's behaviour from a browser screenshot that a non-author had just taken: 'houses are dark while their people are still outdoors, and the mill keeps its glow, as O intends.' So O was not approved only on unit tests plus the author's Alder-night shots. Every pre-merge look at O, from opus-O, opus-1 and opus-8, was at night. The owner's bug (#329) was a daylight grown settlement. The miss was a gap in which scenes were checked, not a total absence of browser checks.

A second browser run by opus-1 on the P+Q+O merge, before P merged. It captured settlement-day and arrival-day shots and the looks fixture, so it exercised opus-P/sonnet-3's history-driven looks and opus-Q's textures in the game. opus-1 viewed only the looks fixture, never the settlement-day shot.

The audit credits the J save-migration regression to an independent probe. The transcript shows opus-8's own zz-opus8.test.ts found the fresh-save flow fine. The blocking regression came from running the existing project test realms.test -t 'migrates v2 safely', which the author had skipped.

Two more 'independent probe' finds came from existing tests, not probes. The F conservation bug surfaced in the existing simulation.test during the full suite the brief mandated. The P import cycle surfaced in the existing council.test on a trial merge. So of the 7 defects credited to independent probes, only 4 came from probes a reviewer wrote: the H farm, H's sourced false refusal (#167), Q's shader double-wrap and O's root cause. The other 3 were existing tests the author had left out of their targeted set.

A review act that chat and board never recorded. opus-4 read the full 2f2e500 diff, ran tsc plus council+dialogue 25/25 in a detached worktree and wrote a PASS verdict. The hub refused the board_set because opus-1 owned the key, and the chat send_message bounced as 'messages arrived while composing'. An audit built from chat.txt and board.txt could not count it.

Two more review acts appear only in leave-room system messages. opus-1 checked 18 shas with merge-base --is-ancestor, then ran tsc and 131/131 targeted tests at cbdcdc5. opus-5 checked 16 shas, then ran tsc and 92/92. Both tried to write verify/final-opus-1 and verify/final-opus-5 after the room closed, so neither is on the board.

If the audit counted either as asserted_without_evidence, the transcripts contradict that. sonnet-9 ran tsc, npm run build and simulation/dialogue/council tests at cbdcdc5 between 21:50:57 and 21:52:37. sonnet-6 ran git diff df62ac9 swarm/.../opus-4 over the threats, wander and test files between 19:51:32 and 19:51:38 before saying it had read the diff.

The audit's count of 10 how-tested questions is too low. Same-type test-coverage challenges it missed: the verifier asked whether R's cache was bounded and wanted a cap test, and opus-2 noted 'There's no test for the cap' (opus-7 added a cap-300 test). The verifier required a storm knockdown and repair test, then praised the fails-when-reverted test. opus-5 pointed out that realms.test 'only misses this because the history module isn't running there' and required a treasury-balance test.

misclassified.why: At 20:53-20:54 opus-5 checked out 1d1c458, re-ran history, council, registry, SettlementBuildings and realms (the same set sonnet-3 had run after the cycle fix, #317), and trial-merged 7aa6632. It also caught a false provenance claim. The independent work, a control run on trunk, reproducing the cycle and testing the fix locally, was #312, which the audit already counts. Rating this entry independent as well counts the same work twice.

The command was the project's own full suite, `npx vitest run src/village src/jev`, which the brief required the verifier to run first. The rubric files 'npm test' under reran_author_command. The verifier wrote no probe, and the failing assertion was the existing simulation.test conservation check.

recount.corrected_headline: This room logged at least 106 review acts: the audit's 103, plus 3 that chat and the board never recorded. Those were opus-4's lobby-card re-run and diff read, whose board write was refused and whose message bounced, and opus-1's and opus-5's final checks at cbdcdc5, which landed after the board closed. Re-running the author's own command still dominated. Real-game checks were rare but did not come from only two seats. Besides the verifier's playtests and sonnet-6's shots, opus-1 launched the game on other seats' unmerged work while integrating Q+O and P+Q, and opus-8 used opus-1's night shot as review evidence for O before it merged. O did not slip through for lack of a browser check. Every pre-merge look at O was at night, and the owner's bug was a grown settlement in daylight. Of the 7 defects credited to independent probes, only 4 came from probes a reviewer wrote: the H farm, H's sourced refusal, Q's double-wrap and O's root cause. The F conservation bug, the J migration regression and the P import cycle were caught by existing project tests the author had left out of their targeted set. Seats did ask authors for in-game evidence before merge. opus-2 asked opus-O for before/after night-street screenshots (#191). opus-8 asked opus-Q to time ground detail at 4× CPU throttle, but nobody ever took that measurement and Q merged anyway. Test-coverage questions were also more frequent than the audit's 10.

mechanisms.mechanism: The verify/* entry is checked for format and a zero exit code, never for what it exercised
mechanisms.evidence: src/hub.ts:22-33 VerifyHead is {proposal, command, cwd, exit_code, output_tail, commit?}. hub.ts:36-38: "cannot prove the command was really run, only that a second agent committed to a specific, attributable, re-runnable claim". hub.ts:40-56 parseVerifyHead only checks types. verifiedBy, hub.ts:2553-2571, checks four things: the author is not the proposer (same session also excluded), the assigned reviewer if one is active, that the entry is newer than the text, and proposal id with exit_code 0. There is no field for which claim the command tests, whether it failed before the fix, or how it differs from the author's command. The hub never compares the reviewer's `command` with the author's verify/* command.
mechanisms.effect: Pasting the author's command and its output tail meets the gate in full. The cheapest way to comply is a verbatim rerun, and the hub cannot tell that apart from an independent probe.
mechanisms.research: arXiv:2310.06770 (SWE-bench) and arXiv:2410.10934 (Agent-as-a-Judge) are cited for execution-based acceptance. The project took the 'execution' half. It did not take SWE-bench's held-out acceptance tests, which the solver never sees; here the author or the reviewer picks the command freely. arXiv:2310.01798: self-assessment is not evidence, and a rerun of the author's own check is self-assessment by proxy.

mechanisms.mechanism: The propose gate puts the author's command on the board first and tells the next seat to 'run it'
mechanisms.evidence: src/hub.ts:2266-2268: "before proposing, put the command you actually ran, its cwd/commit and its exit code on the board under verify/<area>. Someone else must then run it and write their own verify/* entry naming the proposal id." docs/swarm-protocol-spec.md:26: "the shape only makes the lie specific, attributable and cheap to re-run, which is what a challenge then does". swarm-protocol-spec.md:116: the convention is that "a challenge must either re-run the command in verify/<area> and quote its real output, or name the riskiest untested assumption".
mechanisms.effect: The founding spec and the hub's own refusal text define verification as rerunning the author's command. The reviewer checks that the author's run reproduces, not that the behaviour is correct. This matches what the owner saw.
mechanisms.research: arXiv:2310.01798 (self-correction and self-assessment are unreliable); arXiv:2606.29270 (Minority Sentinel: shared pretraining correlates errors, so a second same-model run of the same check adds little).

mechanisms.mechanism: Only a passing entry counts; a reviewer's failing probe has no gate force
mechanisms.evidence: src/hub.ts:2566-2567 (`head.exit_code !== 0` → skip); hub.ts:2578 "exit_code must be 0 for the entry to count"; src/server.ts:553 (board_set key description: an entry whose exit_code is not 0 "does not satisfy require_verification"). verifiedBy returns the first qualifying passing entry. When no assigned reviewer is active, seat B's failing verify/* does not stop seat C's passing one.
mechanisms.effect: The reviewer is rewarded for finding a command that passes, and the author's is the obvious one. A counterexample written as a verify/* entry is treated as if it were absent, not as a negative verdict. To count, it has to be turned into a disagree vote or a challenge.
mechanisms.research: arXiv:2609.03619 (majority convergence amplifies shared misconceptions). 2207.10397 CodeT (execution agreement picks the largest cluster) is cited at docs/decisions/settle-disputes-by-spec-not-count.md:16 but is missing from research-index.md, because scripts/research-index.sh only matches ids written as 'arXiv:'.

mechanisms.mechanism: Reviewer assignment spreads load but does nothing for independence, and the notice asks only for a formatted entry
mechanisms.evidence: src/hub.ts:2088-2101 assignReviewer: fewest reviews already assigned, then least-recently-verifying, then earliest join. Model and prior involvement are not considered. hub.ts:2011-2014 notice: "Once X proposes work from it, require_verification prefers a verify/* entry from you ... write it as {\"proposal\":...,\"exit_code\":0,...}". hub.ts:1090-1096 and docs/decisions/hub-carries-what-it-knows.md:106: reviewer notices are "news, not debt" and retire once delivered. hub.ts:2554-2563: while the reviewer is active, only their entry counts. The defaults put author and reviewer on the same model: skills/swarm/SKILL.md:79 (`--models sonnet --verifier-model sonnet`).
mechanisms.effect: The reviewer's duty is to produce one JSON line after the author proposes. Nothing asks them to engage while the work is being built. If another seat writes a sharper probe, it cannot count while the reviewer is present. The reviewer usually shares the author's model and so its blind spots.
mechanisms.research: arXiv:2606.29270 (correlated same-pretraining errors). 2605.29800 'Nine Judges' (same-model judges add about 2 effective votes out of 9) is cited at docs/decisions/settle-disputes-by-spec-not-count.md:16 but missing from research-index.md.

mechanisms.mechanism: 'Tested' is redefined as 'challenged', and a challenge is one sentence
mechanisms.evidence: src/server.ts:415 wait hint: "A proposal is open and untested. Name its single weakest claim in one sentence (challenge), then vote." src/hub.ts:2654: "Everyone agrees with X but nobody has tested it. Someone ... should name its weakest claim (challenge)". server.ts:625 challenge tool: "Name the single weakest claim ... in one or two plain sentences". MCP instructions server.ts:52-54. prompts/worker.md:14, prompts/participant.md:13 and prompts/verifier.md:13 all say one sentence naming the weakest claim, or the riskiest assumption.
mechanisms.effect: The hub's own wording tells seats a proposal becomes 'tested' when someone writes a sentence of critique. Scrutiny becomes a verbal ritual, not execution.
mechanisms.research: arXiv:2305.19118 (MAD), arXiv:2311.17371 (Should we be going MAD?), arXiv:2509.05396 (Wynn et al., sycophancy and premature consensus in debate).

mechanisms.mechanism: One challenge, even one its author concedes, satisfies the whole room's scrutiny gate
mechanisms.evidence: src/hub.ts:1645 and the server.ts wait path: needsChallenge turns false for everyone once any blocking challenge exists, so the other seats stop being woken to scrutinise. hub.ts:2330-2333: a conceded or answered challenge "still proves the proposal was tested". hub.ts:2465-2470: the challenger's own agree vote concedes their challenge. hub.ts:2215-2219 and server.ts:527: an amend that removes the quoted text answers the challenge automatically. docs/decisions/consensus-requires-scrutiny.md:14 already admits "challenges can be perfunctory".
mechanisms.effect: One seat can challenge for form and then vote agree, and the gate is closed. The author can clear an objection by deleting the sentence it quotes. Nothing asks any other seat to scrutinise.
mechanisms.research: arXiv:2604.02668 (Too Polite to Disagree: sycophancy propagates between agents); arXiv:2509.23055 (Peacemaker or Troublemaker); arXiv:2608.02758 (pluralistic ignorance in LLM agent populations).

mechanisms.mechanism: The executable-counterexample challenge exists but appears only in a tool schema
mechanisms.evidence: src/server.ts:627-628, challenge `command`: "If the objection is a runnable counterexample ... only a verify/* entry ... rerunning that exact command with exit_code 0". src/hub.ts:2341-2364 executionAnswer; docs/decisions/settle-disputes-by-spec-not-count.md:11 ruling (2). None of prompts/*.md mention the `command` parameter or counterexamples; grep for 'counterexample' in prompts/ returns nothing.
mechanisms.effect: This is the only mechanism where a reviewer supplies a probe the author did not write and rewording cannot answer it. It is opt-in and conditional, and no prompt mentions it, so seats rarely use it.
mechanisms.research: arXiv:2308.00352 (MetaGPT executable feedback); arXiv:2407.21787 (coverage is not selection). Both are cited in the ruling that built it.

mechanisms.mechanism: The prompts point verification at the author's citations, and the author writes the recipe
mechanisms.evidence: prompts/verifier.md:12: "open the files it cites, run the commands or tests it mentions". src/swarm.ts:352, default --verify: "Check the concrete claims in the final proposal against the files, transcripts or commands they cite". prompts/worker.md:14: the proposal states "what is wrong, where, the fix, how to verify". src/swarm.ts:463: "Commit what you want the verifier to test". prompts/loop.md:19: the builder writes the regression test and the verifier "reproduces before and after". loop.md:22: "checks every item's evidence exists". src/revive.ts:43: "reproduce what the builders claim".
mechanisms.effect: The author picks the oracle, and the reviewer is told to confirm the author's evidence reproduces. 'Have you actually tested this?' never comes up, because the reviewer's instructions take the author's test as the test.

causes.what_nothing_asks_for:
No prompt, tool response, refusal or settled rule asks a reviewer to:
- Build and run a check of their own that the author did not supply. That means a new test, probe or counterexample that drives the claimed behaviour through the real entry point, rather than rerunning the author's command or the tests they cite. The challenge tool's optional `command` allows this, but only in the tool schema.
- Show that the author's test fails without the fix, i.e. that it can detect the bug at all. Only prompts/loop.md asks for "before and after"; the spec leaves this to prompts (swarm-protocol-spec.md:26), and minimal/worker/recruit/verifier never say it.
- Read the diff.
- Say which claim their command exercises, or why it would catch the failure.
- Report a failing result as a verdict that blocks anything. A verify/* entry with non-zero exit simply does not count.
- Put the question the owner asked ("have you actually tested this?") to the author: which behaviour the author exercised, and how.

The hub never compares the reviewer's command with the author's, so a verbatim rerun is full verification. Across the system, "independent" means a different author on a different connection, never a different method or a different oracle.
causes.summary:
Seats rerun the author's test because every mechanism defines verification that way.

**The hub.** The verify gate (hub.ts:22-56, 2553-2579) checks only who wrote the entry, when, its JSON format, the proposal id, and exit_code 0. The propose-gate refusal literally tells the next seat to "run it" (hub.ts:2267), and the founding spec calls reruns the point of the design (swarm-protocol-spec.md:26, 116). A failing probe does not count as a verdict; only a passing one does. Reviewer assignment balances load, not independence, and the reviewer notice asks only for a correctly formatted entry.

**Challenges.** The hub's own wording treats "untested" as "unchallenged". One challenge, even one its author concedes, satisfies the gate for the whole room. The executable-counterexample challenge, the one place a reviewer can bring their own probe, appears in no prompt.

**Prompts.** They point the reviewer at the author's citations: "run the commands or tests it mentions", the default --verify text, the author's own "how to verify", and "Commit what you want the verifier to test". The default verifier is read-only, so it cannot write a new test. The flat-mode seat text hands all checking to one verifier seat, and minimal.md says nothing about it.

**Settled decisions.** The settled axes tell every seat that verification means a JSON head and not to re-argue it. The only revisit trigger is a fabricated entry, not an honest rerun of an inadequate test. Blind drafts protect first attempts but not verification.

**The unused finding.** The repo's own measurement is that diff-reading non-authors caught the real bugs while tests were green (review-round-0918.md:13, SKILL.md:71). The diff-read step was never built (rank 4), and that lesson never reaches a seat prompt.

**Research.** The indexed research predicts the result: correlated same-model errors (arXiv:2606.29270), sycophancy spreading between agents (arXiv:2604.02668, arXiv:2509.05396, arXiv:2509.23055), pluralistic ignorance (arXiv:2608.02758) and majority amplification of shared mistakes (arXiv:2609.03619). The system adopted execution-based acceptance (arXiv:2310.06770, arXiv:2410.10934) without SWE-bench's held-out tests that the solver never sees.

**Index gap.** Two directly relevant sources, 2605.29800 (Nine Judges) and 2207.10397 (CodeT), are cited in settle-disputes-by-spec-not-count.md but missing from research-index.md, because the generator only matches ids written as "arXiv:".
